# Copilot instructions for this repo

One Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind 4) app serving a 30-day GitHub Copilot training program (Basic: Days 1-10 built, Intermediate/Advanced: 11-30 not yet built — `/days/N` shows a placeholder until `src/days/day-NN/` exists and is registered).

## Build, test, lint

```
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000
npm test                     # node --test over src/days/**/*.test.js
npm run test:seeded          # intentionally-failing tests in *.seeded.js (Day 4 bug) — NOT part of npm test
npm run build                # next build
npm run lint                 # eslint
```

- Run a single test file directly, e.g. `node --test src/days/day-01/order.service.test.js`.
- Lab test files are CommonJS (`require`, no build step) even though the rest of the app is TypeScript/ESM.
- Unfinished lab functions use `{ todo: ... }` node:test stubs so `npm test` stays green; don't "fix" these — they're intentional participant exercises.
- Files named `*.seeded.js` contain deliberate bugs/failures and are excluded from `npm test` on purpose; only `npm run test:seeded` runs them.
- `eslint.config.mjs` ignores `app-track/**` in addition to the eslint-config-next defaults.

## Architecture

- **Day registry pattern**: `src/days/registry.ts` lists all 30 days (level, title, date). `src/days/showcases.tsx` maps a day number to its React showcase component. `src/app/days/[day]/page.tsx` reads both to render `/days/N` — a day with no `showcases.tsx` entry renders a placeholder, not a 404.
- **Day folder**: each `src/days/day-NN/` is self-contained: `DayNN.tsx` (showcase), lab code (`*.service.js` etc.), `*.test.js`, `LAB.md` (mirrors the external lab workbook so the repo works without the website). New days follow this exact pattern (see `docs/BASIC-PLAN.md` for the full Day 1-10 spec).
- **Gating logic** lives in `DayContent` (`src/app/days/[day]/page.tsx`): a day's content is hidden until `isOpen(entry.date)` (`src/lib/schedule.ts`), unless the viewer is an acting facilitator (`src/lib/viewMode.ts`). Reading the session via `auth()` first is deliberate — it forces the rest of the tree dynamic so gated content is never statically prerendered.
- **Facilitator mode** (`?facilitator=1`) reveals answer keys/demo scripts; it's a convenience, not security — keys ship in the page payload, so never treat it as access control.
- **Auth & data**: `src/auth.ts` / `src/proxy.ts` (Auth.js v5, single-tenant Microsoft Entra) gate the whole site. Quiz results and day attendance go to Neon Postgres via `src/lib/db.ts`; tables are created automatically on first use. The server re-grades quiz answers itself (`src/lib/grade.ts`) — never trust client-submitted scores.
- **Optional app track**: `src/app/track/page.tsx` + `src/track/tasks.ts` drive an opt-in cross-day Next.js app build; `app-track/` holds its README, `check-prereqs.mjs`, and seed/paste-in-bug fixtures — separate from the main `src/days/day-NN/` labs.
- Next.js 16 runs with Cache Components enabled: route `params` must be read inside a `Suspense` boundary (see `DayPage`/`DayContent` split in `src/app/days/[day]/page.tsx`) — follow that pattern for any new dynamic route.

## Conventions

- Seeded/example secrets and PII must be obviously fake (`FAKE-...`); this matters most for Day 9 content, which is reviewed for real secrets/PII before each run.
- `AGENTS.md` (regenerated by `next dev`, keep it in commits) says to check `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before any framework-level Next.js change, since this app pins a Next.js version with API/convention differences from older training data.
